etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: First attested 1581, borrowed from French diatribe, from Latin diatriba (“learned discussion or discourse”), from Ancient Greek διατριβή (diatribḗ, “way of spending time, lecture”), from διά (diá, “through”) + τρίβω (tríbō, “to waste, wear out”)
senses: An abusive, bitter verbal or written attack, criticism or denunciation.
A prolonged discourse; a long-winded speech.
